findings.title: Definition of Done box "Required approval is obtained" was checked, and Final Status was set to PASS, while approval has not happened and no verifier is recorded
findings.evidence: private/clio-private/roadmap/phase-100620-retrieval-stage-scores.md, staged diff of the nested private repo: the developer rewrote `- [ ] Required approval is obtained.` to `- [x] Required approval is obtained (downstream pipeline step).` and added the text "(downstream pipeline step)" to make the box true. In the same staged edit the Attribution table still reads `| Adversary | r1 | [TBD] | [TBD] |`, `| Remediator | r1 | [TBD] | [TBD] |`, `| Remedy Approver | r1 | [TBD] | [TBD] |`, `| Finalize | r1 | [TBD] | [TBD] |`, and section 12 still reads `- Verifier: [TBD]`. `### Final Status` was changed from the template `PASS | PASS WITH DOCUMENTED LIMITATIONS | BLOCKED | FAILED` to `PASS`.
findings.requirement_ref: phase doc section 9 "Definition of Done"; phase doc section 12 "Verification Sign-Off"; AGENTS.md "Final Verification" (state clearly what was verified)
findings.recommendation: Leave the approval box unchecked until the remedy approver and finalizer sign, and do not fix `Final Status` to PASS while `Verifier:` is still `[TBD]`. Either mark the box as pending with a pointer to the downstream step, or set Final Status only after a verifier row exists.

findings.title: AC-100620-03 required "Before/after test output" but the phase file supplies only post-change tests; the pre-change fused score was never captured
findings.evidence: phase doc section 9 table row AC-100620-03: `Required Evidence | Before/after test output`. The `Evidence (actual, 2026-09-26)` row for AC-100620-03 cites only post-change tests: `reranker_keeps_scores_and_existing_order_behavior`, `identical_inputs_produce_identical_scores_and_ranks` (crates/clio-retrieve/src/stage_score_tests.rs:262, :300) and `raw_scores_are_recorded_per_list_and_never_change_the_fused_score` (crates/clio-retrieve/src/fusion_tests.rs:73). None of these compares against the pre-change code; `identical_inputs_produce_identical_scores_and_ranks` runs the post-change binary twice. The only pre-change artifact in the run log is a coverage JSON (`/tmp/cov-baseline.json`), not a score snapshot. Task 1 Required Change 4 asks for the fused `score` to stay "byte-for-byte equal to the pre-change value".
findings.requirement_ref: phase doc section 9 AC-100620-03; section 5 Task 1 Required Changes item 4; section 10 "Verification Rule"
findings.recommendation: I verified the claim independently and it holds: building HEAD and the staged tree, then running both `clio recall --output json` binaries against one shared SQLite store, gives bit-identical top-level `score` values (0.01182377049180328, 0.011609345351043642, 0.011448412545316509) and identical ordering and ranks, with the per-hit `scores` object as the only payload difference. Add that before/after output to section 9 as the AC-100620-03 evidence, or state plainly that only post-change determinism plus code inspection was done. The harness is kept at private/clio-private/runs/phase-100620/adversary-compare-pre-post.py and its output at private/clio-private/runs/phase-100620/adversary-pre-post-compare.json.

findings.title: The required Discovery Output reports post-change (and one wrong) test counts as "before the change", and quotes a coverage total that does not match the gate output
findings.evidence: phase doc section 4 `Discovery Output (implementation time, 2026-09-26)`: "**Existing test coverage:** 154 `clio-retrieve` tests, 346 `clio-mcp` tests, 64 `clio-lib` read tests before the change". Measured: `git grep -c '#\[test\]' HEAD -- 'crates/clio-retrieve/**'` totals 150; the worktree totals 162; the staged diff adds exactly 12. For clio-mcp, HEAD totals 343, the worktree 346, the staged diff adds 3. So 154 is neither the pre-change nor the post-change count, and 346 is the post-change count. The run log repeats the error at the intermediate step: `private/clio-private/runs/phase-100620/developer-task-r1.log` line "core verify: ... `cargo test -p clio-retrieve --locked` 154 passed" (that step added 1 test to a 150-test baseline, so 151). Separately, AC-100620-07 quotes `TOTAL lines 97.87%`; my own `make coverage` on the same tree prints `coverage-guard: TOTAL lines 97.88% functions 98.70%` and the raw JSON is 48422/49472 = 97.8776%.
findings.requirement_ref: phase doc section 4 "Discovery Output" (must report existing test coverage) and section 8 "Verification Rule"
findings.recommendation: Correct the two pre-change counts to 150 (`clio-retrieve`) and 343 (`clio-mcp`), or relabel 162/346 as post-change counts. Re-quote the coverage total from the guard's own output so the number in the phase file is the one the gate printed.

findings.title: No binding-level or real-binary evidence ever shows a populated `semantic`, so the AC-100620-06 parity claim is only exercised on the null case
findings.evidence: Every binding test deliberately runs with no embedder, and the tests say so. `crates/clio-mcp/src/read_scores_tests.rs:30-31` ("no embedder is resolved, so the dense arm is off and `semantic` must be `null`") and `:194` (`assert!(!state.pipeline.dense_available, "no embedder configured: dense arm is off")`). `crates/clio-lib/src/cli_read_tests.rs:162` asserts `scores["semantic"].is_null(), "no embedder: {hit}"`. The developer's real-binary evidence quoted under AC-100620-02 is `"scores":{"final":0.0118...,"keyword":1e-6,"reranker":null,"semantic":null}`. My own pre/post binary run also produced `"semantic":null` for every hit. `semantic` is populated only in the in-process `clio-retrieve` tests (crates/clio-retrieve/src/stage_score_tests.rs:171 and :207-211). AC-100620-06's evidence therefore says "exact `semantic`/`keyword`" parity while `semantic` is null on both sides. Section 9 `Verification limits` discloses only the Postgres gap, not this one.
findings.requirement_ref: phase doc section 8 T100620-01 and T100620-06; section 9 AC-100620-06
findings.recommendation: Add one binding test (or a real-binary run) with a stub embedder so a populated `semantic` is observed in the MCP and CLI JSON, and add this limit to `Verification limits`. The transform itself is already pinned by unit tests and by crates/clio-retrieve/src/stage_score_tests.rs:207-211 against a real anti-parallel vector fixture, so the residual risk is low.

findings.title: `finalize.rs` and `stage_score.rs` both claim ownership of the `scores` object
findings.evidence: `crates/clio-retrieve/src/finalize.rs:14` under `## Owns`: "The per-hit `scores` object attached to each `ScoredHit`". `crates/clio-retrieve/src/stage_score.rs:11` under `## Owns`: "`HitScores`, the nested `scores` object serialized on every `ScoredHit`", while its `## Does not own` (line 17) excludes "Final hit assembly (`finalize`)". Two modules claim the same artifact.
findings.requirement_ref: AGENTS.md "File Header" ("The responsibility and ownership statements MUST accurately describe the actual module"); phase doc section 5 Task 3 ("Remove the two-parallel-fields smell: one structure holds per-arm rank and per-arm score provenance")
findings.recommendation: Split the claim: `stage_score.rs` owns the `HitScores` type, its field contract, and the dense transform; `finalize.rs` owns populating the fields from the per-arm signals. Say so in both headers so the next reader has one place to look.

findings.title: The same doc still carries a second, now-stale output-stability claim that this phase invalidates
findings.evidence: `docs/recall-scope-and-dedup.md:31`: "`balanced` is the neutral default: with no scope preset and no `prefer_consolidated`, it applies no cap, so an unchanged bank keeps its pre-existing recall output." After this phase an unchanged bank's recall output is not its pre-existing one: every hit now carries `scores`. The developer corrected the stricter claim on line 35 ("keeps its pre-scope shape apart from the always-present per-hit `scores` object") but left line 31 as is.
findings.requirement_ref: phase doc section 5 Task 2 Required Changes item 5 ("Update `docs/recall-scope-and-dedup.md` where it promises a byte-for-byte payload for plain calls"); section 9 Definition of Done "Documentation is updated where required"
findings.recommendation: Qualify line 31 the same way as line 35, for example "...keeps its pre-existing recall output apart from the always-present per-hit `scores` object". The claim is about the dedup cap, so only the payload wording needs the qualifier.

findings.title: `mcp_read_conformance.rs` was held at exactly 450 lines by shortening an existing comment, which AGENTS.md discourages, and the file now has zero headroom
findings.evidence: `crates/clio-mcp/tests/mcp_read_conformance.rs` is 450 lines. The staged diff replaces the two-line comment "Non-deterministic across runs: wall-clock timing and recency-boosted / floats differ in their last bits even with identical data." with the single line "Non-deterministic across runs: timing and recency-boosted float bits." The developer's run log states the reason: "rustfmt pushed mcp_read_conformance.rs to 451 lines, so shortened the volatile-mask comment by one line to keep the file at exactly 450." The same phase also pushed `crates/clio-lib/src/cli_read_tests.rs` to 449 lines. The required edit itself was necessary and correct: `scores.final` mirrors the wall-clock-sensitive `score` and had to join the volatile mask at line 209.
findings.requirement_ref: AGENTS.md "Source File Size Constraint" item 4 ("Avoid artificial line reduction through compressed formatting, removal of meaningful documentation, or omission of required tests")
findings.recommendation: No 450-line violation exists today, so this is not a gate failure. Split the conformance file (for example move `mask_volatile` plus the read conformance cases into two files) so the next edit has headroom, instead of shrinking a comment to buy one line.
